source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi,

Thanks for getting back to me.

What I need is someone to take the existing report and turn it into a polished, premium, editable report template that feels like a professional paid assessment.

The current report already exists, so this is not a full copywriting project. The main work is improving the design, layout, structure, and editability.

The key things I need are:

\- A stronger front page

I want the first page to include a prominent score/dashboard panel that shows the customer's vehicle security score, risk band, exposure level, priority level, main reason for the rating, and primary weaknesses. The customer should immediately understand their result upon opening the report.

\- Consistent header and footer

The report should have a clean, consistent header and footer across all pages. This should include details such as the report name, report ID, vehicle group, confidential/restricted status, assessment date, and page number.

\- Scoring summary section

I need a clear scoring table showing the main scoring categories, the maximum score, the customer score, and the total score. This needs to make the assessment feel more transparent and professional.

\- Recommended upgrade path

The recommendations should be presented clearly, ideally in order of priority, such as immediate actions, priority upgrades, and secondary upgrades. The report needs to feel practical and action-led, not just informational.

\- Editable templates

This is very important. I need the final report files to be editable so I can update them for different customers. I need to be able to change details such as vehicle registration, assessment date, report ID, vehicle group, security score, risk band, category scores, weaknesses, recommendations, and customer-specific notes.

\- Multiple report versions

I want editable versions of the report templates for RR01, RR02, RR03, and RR04 so that I can select the appropriate template based on the customer's score/risk level.

The final files need to be easy for me to edit and export as a PDF. Canva or PowerPoint may be best, but I'm open to your recommendation if you think another format would be more suitable.

Please can you let me know:

\- Whether this is the type of project you can help with
\- What file format you would recommend
\- What you would need from me before starting
\- Estimated cost
\- Estimated timescale

Whether the final files would include all fonts, icons and design assets needed for future editing
I can send over the existing sample report and any reference images once I know this is a good fit.

Thanks

value_updates.identifier_requirement: Provide an editable report ID in the consistent report framing for the RR01, RR02, RR03, and RR04 templates.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi,

Thank you for sending over the updated report design. The overall direction is much stronger now, and I'm happy with the general look and feel, so I do not want to redesign it from scratch.

I would like to make a final round of refinements to improve readability, consistency, and the overall commercial finish before I sign it off.

The main changes I'd like are:

1\. Make the front-page score more dominant.

Please make the "22/100" score slightly larger and give it more breathing room so it feels more like the main dashboard result. The customer should immediately notice the score and risk outcome when they open the report.

2\. Rename "Security Score" to "Vehicle Security Score"

On the front page, please change the heading from "Security Score" to "Vehicle Security Score" to make it feel more complete and professional.

3\. Simplify the "What Caused This Result" section.

The wording is good, but the dark blue panel currently feels quite text-heavy. Please reduce this section into shorter, easier-to-scan bullet points. For example:

\- No independent immobilisation
\- No circular steering lock
\- No live-location tracking
\- Storage location is being overvalued
\- Owner security habits reduce protection

The longer explanation can remain elsewhere in the report if needed. Still, page one should feel more immediate and easy to read.

4\. Remove placeholder text

Please remove any placeholder text such as "Click to enter a date." This should either be replaced with the actual assessment date or a clean editable placeholder such as "\[Assessment Date\]".

5\. Check report code consistency

Please check that the report code is consistent throughout. I noticed some areas may show "PR-01". This should be "RR-01" throughout unless there is a specific reason for using something different.

6\. Clean up the vehicle group section

The checkboxes next to Range Rover / Range Rover Sport / Defender make the section feel slightly like a form rather than a completed report. Please either make this a cleaner fixed line, such as:

"Vehicle Group: Range Rover / Range Rover Sport / Defender"

or make it customer-specific, for example:

"Vehicle Assessed: Range Rover Sport"

7\. Add a subtle header to pages 2 onwards

The footer works well, but I'd also like a subtle header across the internal pages for consistency. Something simple would be fine, such as:

"Vehicle Theft Risk Assessment | RR-01 | Confidential"

This should be subtle and not take up too much space.

8\. Refine the red distribution warning on the final page

I like the idea of the warning section, but the red block currently feels a little too heavy. Please keep the warning, but make it slightly more refined and less visually dominant, while still making it clear that the report is confidential and for limited distribution.

Overall, I'm happy with the design direction. I want this final round to focus on polish, readability, consistency and making the report feel like a premium paid assessment.

Please let me know if the above changes are clear and when you expect to send the revised version.

Thanks

value_updates.identifier_consistency: Use RR-01 throughout the RR01 report rather than PR-01, including the internal-page header.

source_message.text:
Hi,

Thank you for sending the updated files. The main report band corrections have now been made, and the front-page titles look much better.

There are just a couple of final amendments I’d like made before I sign off the files:

**\- Footer report codes**

The main report codes and internal headers now appear correct, but the footers on RR02, RR03 and RR04 still appear to show:

“RR-01 | 21 July 2026”

Please can you update the footer report code across each report so it matches the correct report version:

RR02 footer: RR-02 | 21 July 2026
RR03 footer: RR-03 | 21 July 2026
RR04 footer: RR-04 | 21 July 2026

**\- RR04 “What Matters Most” wording**

In RR04, the current wording says:

“The following controls would make the greatest difference to this vehicle’s current exposure.”

As RR04 is the lower-exposure report, please change this to:

“The following controls are most important to maintaining this vehicle’s lower exposure profile.”

**\- RR04 “What Owners Often Overestimate” wording**

In RR04, the wording currently says:

“This matters because false confidence is one of the clearest features of a severe exposure setup.”

As RR04 is not a severe exposure setup, please change this to:

“This matters because false confidence can weaken an otherwise strong security setup over time.”

Please **double-check** these changes have been made before re-sending and I will be able to sign off.

Thanks
